derivations.quote: Tensor this identity over the axes. Put $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$ (a permutation, not a ring), $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$. By the product rule the left sides combine to $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$, and the right sides to $\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ times $d$ factors $2^{2\alpha^2}$, so $RF_{\boldsymbol s}=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ with $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$.

For a unit $c$ modulo $q$, let $(R_cz)_j=z_{cj}$. Substituting $h=ck$ in the Fourier sum, with $h$ the summation index, gives $F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+$. Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$ by the coprimality assumed, and $R$ applies $R_{t_i}$ on axis $i$, so tensoring gives $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$. A permutation commutes with pointwise products, so the left side is $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\cdot F_{\boldsymbol s}v)=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\cdot F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$. The normalized convolution rule is $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ and $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$, so this equals $\frac1SF_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=u*v/S^2$.
